title: Chords
intro: A chord is three or more notes sounded together. Tonal harmony is built from triads, chords stacked in thirds, and from the seventh chords that add one more third on top.

blocks.text: A triad stacks two thirds on a root: root, third and fifth. The kinds of third decide its quality:

items: Major: major third + minor third (C E G). Root to fifth is a perfect fifth. Bright, stable.
Minor: minor third + major third (C E♭ G). Perfect fifth. Darker, still stable.
Diminished: minor + minor (C E♭ G♭). Diminished fifth. Tense, unstable.
Augmented: major + major (C E G♯). Augmented fifth. Unsettled, symmetric.

blocks.text: Building a triad on each degree of a major scale, using only the scale's notes, gives a fixed pattern of qualities: I major, ii minor, iii minor, IV major, V major, vi minor, vii° diminished. In C major that is C, Dm, Em, F, G, Am, B°. Roman numerals name the chord by its scale degree, so the same progression can be talked about in any key: I–IV–V–I is C–F–G–C in C and G–C–D–G in G.
In minor (using harmonic minor's raised 7̂ for V and vii°, as composers usually did) the pattern is i, ii°, III, iv, V, VI, vii°. In A minor: Am, B°, C, Dm, E, F, G♯°.

examples.label: I ii iii IV V vi vii° I

blocks.text: Adding a third above the fifth gives a seventh chord. Five qualities are common, each named by its triad and the interval from root to seventh:

items: Major seventh (Cmaj7): major triad + major 7th, C E G B. Soft and lush; I and IV in major.
Dominant seventh (C7): major triad + minor 7th, C E G B♭. Contains a tritone (E–B♭) that drives it to resolve; built on V.
Minor seventh (Cm7): minor triad + minor 7th, C E♭ G B♭. ii, iii and vi in major.
Half-diminished seventh (Cø7 or Cm7♭5): diminished triad + minor 7th, C E♭ G♭ B♭. vii in major, ii in minor.
Fully diminished seventh (C°7): diminished triad + diminished 7th, C E♭ G♭ B𝄫 (sounds like A). Stacked minor thirds; vii° in minor.

blocks.text: In a major key the diatonic sevenths are Imaj7, ii7, iii7, IVmaj7, V7, vi7, viiø7. The only dominant seventh is on V, which is part of why V7 identifies the key so strongly.

Play every triad in a key with the right hand fingers 1–3–5, stepping up the scale: the shape stays the same while the qualities change under it. Then add the left hand playing just the root an octave or two lower. Close position (all notes within an octave) is clear in the middle of the keyboard; below about C3 thirds turn muddy, so the left hand plays roots, fifths and octaves there.

items: Inversions and Figured Bass (#/arts/music-theory/chords/inversions): which note is in the bass, and how it was written in the Baroque.
Extended and Altered Chords (#/arts/music-theory/chords/extended-and-altered): ninths, elevenths, thirteenths, suspensions, added notes and chord symbols.

blocks.title: Qualities
blocks.text: Name each triad: D F♯ A; E G B♭; F A C♯; G♯ B D♯.
solution: D F♯ A: M3 + m3 = D major. E G B♭: m3 + m3 = E diminished. F A C♯: M3 + M3 = F augmented. G♯ B D♯: m3 + M3 = G♯ minor.

blocks.title: Roman numerals
blocks.text: In B♭ major, spell ii, IV and V7.
solution: B♭ major: B♭ C D E♭ F G A. ii = C E♭ G (C minor). IV = E♭ G B♭. V7 = F A C E♭.
blocks.answer: Cm; E♭; F7 (F A C E♭)

blocks.title: Seventh quality
blocks.text: Which seventh chord is B D F A, and where does it occur diatonically?
solution: B–D–F is a diminished triad and B–A a minor seventh: half-diminished, Bø7. It is viiø7 in C major and iiø7 in A minor.
blocks.answer: Bø7: viiø7 in C major, iiø7 in A minor
